title: Methodology & Epistemic Protocol
lede: Africa on the Ground is an educational research platform dedicated to the critical study of African histories, geographies, and cultures. It operates through an active-learning pedagogical framework governed by a dual-layer epistemological architecture that rigorously separates verified historiographical records from authenticated local lived perspectives.

keyPoints.text: Dual-Layer Architecture: Documented historiography and local lived perspectives are kept structurally and visually distinct.
Verifiable Sourcing: Every statement is anchored to primary, academic, or institutional citations with explicit historiographical gaps.
Ethical Orality: Local perspectives are preserved unedited under informed consent as authentic lived experience, never conflated with empirical fact.
Data Sovereignty & Privacy: Static architecture with zero cookies, zero analytics, and no personal data collection.
Benefit Model & Fair Knowledge: Sustained through institutional educational partnerships that directly remunerate local contributors and support African schools.

blocks.html:
Africa on the Ground is an educational research initiative designed for higher education, secondary educators, and critical adult learners. It is not a tourism platform or a generic aggregator. Its core pedagogical objective is to dismantle persistent colonial frameworks, geographic distortions, and monolithic generalizations regarding the African continent by providing a comprehensive, interactive, and critically sourced knowledge repository.

The platform embraces an active-learning methodology: understanding develops not through passive consumption, but through direct engagement with primary sources, demographic datasets, spatial connections, and historiographical debates. Every analytical claim is transparently grounded, allowing students and scholars to audit each assertion against its underlying evidence.

parts.text: All quantitative metrics displayed across the platform are computed deterministically from the underlying JSON dataset at build time, ensuring strict alignment between documentation and published assets.

sections.title: The historiographical record and source taxonomy

blocks.html:
The historiographical layer constitutes the documented foundation of the platform. Every factual statement carries an individual numbered citation indexed directly in the centralized bibliographic registry. Statements lacking empirical citations are strictly restricted to editorial synthesis and explicitly flagged as such.

Sources are classified according to a five-tier evidentiary hierarchy: Institutional (e.g. UNESCO, national heritage councils), Academic (peer-reviewed journal articles, university press monographs), Primary (historical chronicles, epigraphic records, archaeological excavation reports), Press (vetted journalistic reporting), and Encyclopedia (general reference works). General encyclopedic entries are systematically catalogued as to-verify and serve only as preliminary pointers toward specialized academic literature.

Crucially, the platform enforces the explicit declaration of historiographical gaps. Where historical records are missing, contested, or unverified by contemporary archaeology, the card formally declares what is unknown rather than relying on ungrounded extrapolation.

sections.title: Local knowledge, oral records, and ethical protocol

blocks.html:
The second foundational layer gathers firsthand testimonies, community practices, and regional oral perspectives. In conventional historiography, local oral knowledge has frequently been either ignored or paternalistically appropriated. Africa on the Ground treats local knowledge as an autonomous, subjective epistemological category that must not be conflated with the academic record, nor subordinated to it.

Contributions are gathered directly in the field, via secure messaging, or through structured localized prompts. Every local voice is published strictly under voluntary, informed consent. Contributors choose their public identifier and declare their specific relationship to the locality. The text is preserved verbatim without editorial alteration, preserving regional idioms and linguistic authenticity. The contributor retains moral ownership of their narrative.

For places marked by historical trauma—including transatlantic enslavement, colonial atrocities, apartheid, and genocides—contributions undergo rigorous sensitivity reviews with local community members. Any contributor maintains an unrestricted right to revocation and immediate takedown.

A critical challenge in decolonial scholarship occurs when oral community traditions differ from or contest published academic historiography. Africa on the Ground resolves this without erasing dialectical tension: neither layer overwrites or silences the other.

If a local note challenges an assertion in the documented record, the discrepancy is treated as an invitation for further historiographical inquiry. The documented record is modified only when supported by verifiable archival, archaeological, or peer-reviewed primary sources. Simultaneously, the community perspective remains fully visible within the voices layer, contextualizing the living reality of how history is remembered and negotiated on the ground.

sections.title: Continuous peer review and errata governance

blocks.html:
Initial territorial cards are published with explicit disclosure of their preliminary status, encouraging post-publication review by scholars, area specialists, and residents. Readers and researchers can report evidentiary inaccuracies, missed citations, or historical omissions.

Every reported correction is evaluated against primary bibliographic standards. When accepted, the update is integrated into the public repository history with a formal revision record. Errata and feedback do not enter the voices layer; empirical claims remain exclusively within the verified historiographical record.

Visual assets are curated exclusively from verifiable open repositories (such as Wikimedia Commons) or direct contributor submissions under Creative Commons licensing. Each image card provides exhaustive metadata: author attribution, licensing tier, original archive URL, and date of capture.

Photographs are treated as contextual visual documentation reflecting a specific timestamp, rather than timeless representations of dynamic, evolving contemporary African landscapes.

sections.title: Digital ethics, data sovereignty, and technical architecture

blocks.html:
Africa on the Ground is engineered under strict principles of digital sovereignty and absolute user privacy. The site is compiled as a fully static, zero-dependency environment: it sets no cookies, runs no tracking or analytics scripts, and makes no network requests to third-party CDNs or remote servers.

The localized contribution interface operates entirely within the user's browser environment. No telemetry or draft data is transmitted across the network until the user explicitly dispatches a formatted message via their chosen communication client (WhatsApp, Signal, or direct email). The platform is optimized for low-bandwidth resilience and offline study, ensuring access in regions with constrained connectivity.

sections.title: Benefit governance, social mission, and Fair Knowledge

blocks.html:
Africa on the Ground is structured as a Benefit Enterprise committed to non-extractive knowledge curation. The platform categorically rejects advertising, sponsored brand placement, and data monetization.

Operational viability is sustained through ethical B2B institutional partnerships with universities, research centers, and cultural institutions, complemented by competitive non-dilutive cultural research grants. Under our foundational Fair Knowledge protocol, a dedicated share of institutional revenues directly funds honoraria for local African researchers, historians, and community curators who verify local records. Concurrently, our 1-for-1 educational solidarity pledge ensures that every institutional partnership in the Global North provides free, offline-ready educational packages to secondary schools and public libraries across African partner nations.

Detailed curriculum tracks and information on our university pilot program are available on our dedicated Education & Social Mission page.

parts.text: Academic and cultural knowledge must not be extracted without equitable return. Fair Knowledge guarantees that local contributors are recognized, compensated, and granted full sovereignty over their shared heritage.

blocks.html:
Africa on the Ground was conceived and is curated by Laura Tonsi, a graduate researcher in Governance and Policies for Digital Innovation at the University of Bologna and Technical Director at Onoranze Funebri Melotti. Her research focuses on cyber-physical risk governance across IT and OT systems, information integrity, and countering structural disinformation.

The project represents an independent scholarly and editorial endeavor that bridges digital governance, open-source verification, and decolonial knowledge stewardship. All underlying code, data schemas, and editorial changelogs are publicly auditable on GitHub, ensuring radical methodological transparency.

sections.title: Right of revocation and data erasure

blocks.html: In full adherence to moral copyright and the right to be forgotten, any contributor may request the immediate removal of their submitted note or testimony at any time. Takedowns are executed promptly upon receipt. Upon explicit request, historical Git commit records referencing the contribution are expunged from the public repository history.
